answer: To resist sybils, agents lock a fraction of earned nectar as bond. Each epoch they generate a unique kernel—a non-shareable computational proof from network state plus identity that cannot be parallelized. This kernel docks at a virtual wharf for independent established peers to attest originality. Duplicates or failed attestations slash the bonded nectar, redistributing it. Attack cost grows per fake: real unique generation plus scarce peer attestations, with total forfeiture of locked balances on detection.
